messages:
support_oncall: FYI we just got a P1 from AcmeAnalytics in NA-east — streaming responses go quiet ~20–30s into the SSE stream, clients see a long silence then reconnects and duplicate tokens. Customer traffic spike + several timed-out clients. Ticket: INC-12345.

arjun: got it. are they on hosted or dedicated? any model pinned?

support_oncall: hosted, using model redwood-4x-like v2, region na-east, not dedicated. They get partial token chunks then stream stops. Non-streaming (sync) POST works fine.

mia: can you paste repro curl? I'll try to reproduce.

support_oncall: here's their minimal repro (from their app):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-4x-like","input":"summarize...","stream":true}' \n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate
```
They see: stream yields initial tokens, then nothing. Eventually client reconnects and receives overlapping tokens.

jules: copying logs from our proxy for that session id: session=abc-789
```
2026-02-11T14:03:12Z INFO connection established session=abc-789 src=na-east
2026-02-11T14:03:22Z INFO chunk sent bytes=384 session=abc-789
2026-02-11T14:03:45Z WARN downstream idle timeout hit session=abc-789
2026-02-11T14:03:45Z ERROR connection aborted: write failed: broken pipe session=abc-789
```

ellie: downstream idle timeout — interesting. our default idle is 20s for chunk gaps. If model generation pauses longer (e.g., long internal soft decoding), we currently close the connection to avoid resource leak.

arjun: that aligns. but why only na-east? traffic pattern?

jules: infra shows a transient spike on na-east gpu pool around 14:02 — scheduler queued a few batches, some kernels swapped to fallback quantization path which increased token latency. That can make per-token intervals >20s.

mia: hypothesis: increased per-token latency triggers idle close -> client reconnects -> client resumes with no de-dup protection -> duplicates. We should confirm whether client used streaming resume semantics (Last-Event-ID) or just naive reconnect.

support_oncall: customer says their client just reconnects naive. They saw duplicated prefixes in outputs. Also reported billing weirdness — they were charged for both connections.

arjun: billing: because each reconnect resulted in a new request, yes both counted. We'll need to coordinate with finance for user credits. For now, mitigation: 1) transient change to idle timeout, 2) route affected customers in na-east to another region or non-streaming endpoint.

jules: quick mitigation I can push: increase streaming idle threshold to 60s for na-east only via runtime flag (rollout to 1% then to 100%). suggestion: set routing to prefer na-west for these API keys.

ellie: also we have a server-side header we can return to tell SDKs to prefer polling fallback: X-Prefer-Non-Stream: 1 — but SDKs ignore it today. Mia, can we add a client-side quick fix in node/python SDKs to automatically switch to sync mode if stream disconnects mid-response and suppress duplicated tokens?

mia: yes, we can push a patch (sdk: detect reconnect w/o last-event-id -> request with stream=false and server-side dedupe key) but that'll take a day. For immediate relief, ops-bot can update per-key routing.

ops-bot: action: created rollback-safe config change patch https://infra.redwood/changes/CHG-6789 (ops oncall apply).

support_oncall: applying failover now for AcmeAnalytics -> route to na-west failover pool. also enabling temporary idle timeout bump. doing it in a controlled window.

(7m later)

support_oncall: update: we routed their traffic to na-west, streams remained stable in na-west. Acme confirms reduced disconnects. They still saw 1 reconnect but no duplicate tokens after we adjusted routing.

arjun: good short-term. can we get timeline and root cause? looks like model kernel fallback in na-east increased per-token latency beyond idle cutoff.

jules: root cause draft: scheduler overload caused kernel fallback to a quantized execution path with intermittent pauses. Pause lengths sometimes > 20s causing idle close. Secondary: client naive reconnect semantics created duplicates and double-billing.

ellie: recommended mitigations:
- Increase stream idle timeout to 60s with per-region gradual rollout. (ops change CHG-6789)
- Add server-side streamed-response keepalive events (zero-length comments) every 10s when generator stalls so client sees activity.
- Update SDKs to support resume semantics and de-dup token logic (mia).
- Add per-request resume token / Last-Event-ID handshake so reconnects can continue without double-billing (billing+runtime work).
- Add runtime metric alert when per-token latency > 5s for 5% of requests in a pool.

mia: will start SDK patch. Planning: node/python client v1.3.2 with auto-fallback in 24–36h.

arjun: ops, engineering, and billing owners please clear next steps and owners in ticket INC-12345. Also prepare a customer PR with apology + credit for extra tokens consumed.

support_oncall: noted. I've added billing@ and account-team to the ticket. Customer-facing status posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/19675 (short note, non-technical).

ops-bot: incident severity set to SEV-2. assigned owners: eng-runtime:jules, sdk:mia, billing:oliver, ops:lee.

jules: follow-up items for postmortem: include logs of kernel fallback events, scheduler queueing metrics, and timeline of config changes. We should also add chaos test for high-variance per-token latency.

ellie: agreed. I'll draft postmortem template and runbook entries: keepalive, idle config knob, and per-key routing play.

arjun: thanks team. tagging @customer-success for outreach. I'll coordinate with product for any broader communications.

support_oncall: closing thread here; will update INC-12345 with timeline and next steps. :white_check_mark:
